title: Natural tensor pairing on derived module homology with cycle normalization
statement: For a commutative ring k in universe u and a chosen derived category of ModuleCat k in universe u, use derived homology [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor] and the K-flat derived monoidal tensor for modules as in the generic construction [lem-sc-source-kflat-tensor-left-triangulated]. There is a family of k-bilinear maps from H^p(A) and H^q(B) to H^(p+q)(A tensor-derived B), for arbitrary derived objects A,B and nonnegative p,q. It is natural in both objects. For arbitrary integer cochain complexes K,L and cycles a,b in degrees p,q, there is a total tensor cycle z whose component is the (p,q)-summand inclusion of a tensor b. Applying H^(p+q) of the lax localization comparison to the family evaluated on the localized classes of a,b gives the localized class of z. Localized cycle class is the inverse homologyFunctorFactors component applied to homology projection. This is precisely Nonempty CupDerivedHomologyTensor k.

source.place: Section 15.64, equation-simple-tor-product; Tag 0FKU first paragraphs and proof of Lemma 20.31.1

proof.text: Represent H^p(A) by morphisms from the shifted rank-one free module k[-p]. Projectivity of k identifies these morphisms bijectively with homology, including for unbounded A. Tensor representing maps, precompose with the canonical shifted-unit tensor identification and transport back to homology. Additivity and k-linearity give the required bilinear family; composition gives its naturality. Use the natural linear equivalence and its explicit cocycle formula of lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability, and the normalized isomorphism e of lem-sc-module-cup-shifted-unit-tensor.

For complexes K,L, take the single-complex maps with components the supplied cycles. Their tensor followed by the lax localization comparison is the localization of the tensor of these maps. Its degree p+q component is exactly the tensor summand of a tensor b. The signed Leibniz rule makes it a cycle. The homology factorization of Q identifies its class with the asserted on_cycles value. This includes p=0, q=0, zero complexes, and zero cycles. The representative compatibility is exactly the generator formula and Q(h) identity in lem-sc-module-cup-shifted-unit-tensor, followed by the on_cycles clause of lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability.
